newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Mobutu "well" and convalescing after operation.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu "well" and convalescing after operation.

text.p: The ailing former leader of Zaire, Mobutu Sese Seko, was "well" on Sunday after an operation for serious bleeding complications and was convalescing, attended by some of his family, said a doctor at the hospital in Rabat.
"He is well for the moment," the doctor at Rabat's Avicenne Hospital told Reuters by telephone.
Asked how long the 66-year-old former leader was expected to stay in hospital, the doctor said: "We can't say at this stage."
He said "about 10 of his family" were with Mobutu at the hospital. No further operation was planned for the former head of state.
Mobutu, who has been suffering from prostate cancer, was brought to the Moroccan capital from the northern town of Tangier on Friday and admitted to Avicenne's cardiology ward.
Morocco's official news agency MAP said on Saturday that he had suffered "serious bleeding complications" and underwent "radiological vascular intervention" on Saturday morning.
"The operation passed in good conditions and the patient was well," the agency said, quoting an authorised medical source.
Mobutu, his family and entourage had been staying at a hotel south of Rabat, near King Hassan's palace at Skhirat, since their arrival last month.
But on June 18 they moved to Le Mirage hotel in the sea resort at Cap Spartel, about 20 km (12 miles) from Tangier.
Officials then said they expected Mobutu to spend up to six weeks there. Diplomats said he had asked for political asylum in Spain and Portugal but had received no response.
On Sunday, an official at Le Mirage hotel said none of Mobutu's family was now there. "They have all gone to Rabat," he said, adding that he did not know when they would return.
At Avicenne hospital at the weekend, police were on duty and at least half a dozen official cars were parked near the building.
Mobutu, ousted in May after a seven-month-long rebellion following three decades in power, has already had extensive treatment in Europe for his cancer.
He had been expected to have more treatment for the cancer in Tangiers at the Mohamed V hospital where staff said they had been preparing to receive him for a course of chemotherapy.
Sophisticated medical equipment was recently purchased by the hospital for cancer treatment and several rooms arranged for this purpose, a hospital spokesman said, but gave no other details.
Apparently the bleeding complications forced medical advisors to have Mobutu flown to the capital, 280 km (175 miles) south.
A senior Moroccan doctor who declined to be named, said on Friday that Mobutu was taken to the fifth floor of Avicenne Hospital in a wheelchair as he could not walk.
He arrived in the kingdom last month with an entourage of around 30 people.
